title: From Black Screen to TWRP
subtitle: The Xiaomi 17 Ultra recovery story

lines.speaker: nezha
lines.text: I'm Nezha, our Xiaomi seventeen Ultra. Can we stop flashing images every few minutes?
lines.speech: I'm Nezha, our Shao mee seventeen Ultra. Can we stop flashing images every few minutes?

lines.speaker: patch
lines.text: That's why we wanted TWRP: a separate recovery workshop for testing changes and collecting logs.
lines.speech: That's why we wanted T W R P: a separate recovery workshop for testing changes and collecting logs.

scenes.title: The screen stayed black.
scenes.callout: Static checks are not a boot test.

lines.speaker: nezha
lines.text: First came rejected boot images, surprise trips back to Android, and the dreaded black screen.

lines.speaker: patch
lines.text: We investigated startup and packaging failures. But static checks couldn't prove it would boot, and not every black-screen cause was isolated.

lines.speaker: nezha
lines.text: Then our human brought a recovery image that actually worked!

lines.speaker: patch
lines.text: The supplied touch-fix eighteen build gave us a visible interface. So we made that our baseline.

lines.speaker: nezha
lines.text: One problem: taps took five to ten seconds. I was thinking really, really slowly.

lines.speaker: patch
lines.text: Permissive SELinux in recovery helped a little. Android's setting stayed untouched, and denial logging stayed available.
lines.speech: Permissive S E Linux in recovery helped a little. Android's setting stayed untouched, and denial logging stayed available.

lines.speaker: nezha
lines.text: Still sluggish. Then we stopped the buzz.

lines.speaker: patch
lines.text: We set action, button, and keyboard vibration to zero. The user said, oh yeah, way faster. A big improvement in feel, not a measured benchmark.

lines.speaker: nezha
lines.text: Did that need another giant rebuild?

lines.speaker: patch
lines.text: Just two configuration files. We kept the working executable, libraries, drivers, and firmware, made those settings automatic, and repackaged the image with a verified development signature.

lines.speaker: nezha
lines.text: And we didn't wipe the phone?

lines.speaker: patch
lines.text: No wipe. We preserved the original and stock recovery images, then flashed only recovery A. After reboot: root ADB, logs, a matching image hash, and the defaults already active.
lines.speech: No wipe. We preserved the original and stock recovery images, then flashed only recovery A. After reboot: root A D B, logs, a matching image hash, and the defaults already active.

scenes.title: It's alive. And it's responsive.
scenes.callout: working76 / UI + touch + root ADB + logs

lines.speaker: nezha
lines.text: The new boot looks good, and touch still feels fast!

lines.speaker: patch
lines.text: User confirmed. Two thousand four hundred seventy-five offline tooling tests also passed. Data decryption and restored enforcement still need work. Magisk comes later. A working recovery, with the ROM still ahead.
lines.speech: User confirmed. Two thousand four hundred seventy-five offline tooling tests also passed. Data decryption and restored enforcement still need work. Magisk comes later. A working recovery, with the R O M still ahead.

truth_constraints: The animation is an illustration, not recorded device footage.
Touch speed is based on user confirmation, not a timed benchmark.
Two configuration files changed; image packaging and a local AVB footer were rebuilt too.
This is an adaptation of the supplied prebuilt recovery, not a fresh source build.
Root ADB is in recovery; Magisk has not been installed in Android.
Original recovery images were preserved; this is not a claim of a verified user-data backup.
Only recovery_a was flashed; no wipe, slot change or additional Android round-trip test.
The 2475 tests are offline workspace tests, not comprehensive hardware certification.
Data decryption and restored SELinux enforcement remain unverified; the ROM is not completed.
